candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is neurocysticercosis, a parasitic (Taenia solium) infection causing cysts. Dandy-Walker Malformation is a congenital cerebellar/fourth ventricle developmental defect unrelated to infection. The clinical presentation (adult onset, 3-month history) and posterior fossa cysts in an adult are more consistent with acquired parasitic cysts than a congenital malformation.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Dandy-Walker Malformation is a congenital developmental anomaly, not a parasitic infection

candidate_relations.reason: IIH requires absence of secondary cause. The MRI demonstrates multiple posterior fossa cysts with obstructive hydrocephalus, ruling out IIH. The reference diagnosis is neurocysticercosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: IIH is a diagnosis of exclusion without structural lesions; MRI here shows multiple posterior fossa cysts causing obstructive hydrocephalus

candidate_relations.reason: Same reasoning as C001 but with added hydrocephalus component. Still a congenital developmental diagnosis incompatible with the reference diagnosis of neurocysticercosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Dandy-Walker malformation with obstructive hydrocephalus is a congenital entity; neurocysticercosis is an acquired parasitic infection

candidate_relations.reason: Arachnoid cysts are not caused by Taenia solium and represent a different pathological entity from neurocysticercosis, though both can cause mass effect.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Arachnoid cyst is a benign congenital/acquired CSF-filled cyst, not a parasitic infection

candidate_relations.reason: A Dandy-Walker variant refers to a spectrum of congenital posterior fossa malformations, entirely distinct from the parasitic etiology of neurocysticercosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Dandy-Walker variant is a congenital developmental anomaly, not a parasitic infection

candidate_relations.reason: Hemangioblastoma is a benign vascular neoplasm of the cerebellum, unrelated to Taenia solium infection. Different etiology and pathology from neurocysticercosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Cerebellar hemangioblastoma is a vascular tumor, not a parasitic infection

candidate_relations.reason: Ependymoma is a glial tumor arising from ependymal cells. It is a neoplastic, not parasitic, diagnosis and is incompatible with the reference diagnosis of neurocysticercosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Cystic ependymoma is a neoplastic entity, not a parasitic infection

candidate_relations.reason: Same reasoning as C007. Ependymoma is a tumor and does not represent neurocysticercosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Ependymoma is a neoplastic entity, not a parasitic infection

candidate_relations.reason: Posterior fossa arachnoid cysts are benign, non-parasitic lesions. While they can cause obstructive hydrocephalus similar to the presentation, they are a distinct pathological entity from neurocysticercosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Posterior fossa arachnoid cyst is a benign CSF-filled cyst, not a parasitic infection

case_quality_flags: No candidate correctly identifies neurocysticercosis; all candidates represent alternative diagnoses in the differential
Multiple posterior fossa cysts in an adult with obstructive hydrocephalus and normal CSF strongly supports neurocysticercosis over all listed candidates
Normal CSF (no cells, no protein, no organisms) is consistent with neurocysticercosis in the vesicular stage but does not exclude it
